_note: Terrain grid for the Western Canada (CPR, 1881-87) map. BOARD-REWORK-2: 24 cols x 18 rows, pointy-top odd-r, hex radius 38 -- replaces the 2nd pass's 24x20/radius-40 grid for two independent reasons (Ben's direct feedback after playing the board): (1) HEX=40 spilled tiles past the printed 1700x1400 frame edge (24*40*sqrt(3)+60 = 1722.8, already over-width with zero margin) -- HEX=38 fits with a real ~60px margin on all sides; (2) Vancouver Island (Victoria/Esquimalt/Nanaimo) was removed entirely -- the water-gap crossing didn't fit the board well and wasn't worth keeping -- which also removes the 2-row buffer (rows 18-19) that existed only to give the island room, so rows drop from 20 to 18. In its place, 4 new real 1881-87 towns were added to the northern Edmonton-Battleford-Prince Albert corridor (Victoria Settlement, Fort Pitt, Fort Carlton, Batoche -- see docs/western-canada-board-research.md's board-rework-2 addendum), following the real Carlton Trail route order. The grid was regenerated (scripts/western/gen-terrain.mjs, kept for reference/regeneration) from the updated hand-specified route network, terrain-typed by the same re-derived region rules used in the prior pass (not resized from any older grid), then ONE hex was hand-converted from mountain to plains at (7,8) -- see 'Mountain-band chokepoint relief' below -- to partially address a separate piece of feedback: the Field-Cochrane-Banff-Calgary-Revelstoke-Golden-Kamloops-Gleichen mountain corridor is a single-file chain that could let one company permanently wall off every rival from ever reaching the Pacific coast (the mountain/forest 'one cube per hex, forever' rule is intentional and unchanged, but a single-file gauntlet with zero alternate hex made it too absolute). Legend: O = off-map (water, wilderness, or panel space), P = plains, F = forest, M = mountain, C = city (the city itself comes from cities.json, which must place a city on every C -- see build-map.mjs, which stamps 'terrain:city' over whatever base letter is here; the letter only has to not be 'O').

regions._note: Why each area is the terrain it is. Purely documentation — the generator/build script reads only `grid`. Re-derived for board-rework-2's 24x18 grid from where the actual cities in cities.json now sit (not resized from any older grid's thresholds, and not eyeballed — see gen-terrain.mjs's terrainFor()).
regions.Northern boreal arc: Rows 0-6. Forest. Edmonton (9,2), Victoria Settlement (10,0), Fort Pitt (12,2), Prince Albert (15,3), Battleford (13,5) and Fort Carlton (15,5) all sit in this band, off the CPR mainline proper — matching the research doc's note that this area saw very little of the real 1881-87 construction story and should read as sparse, low-value scenery, same choice as the Canadian board's Shield interior. (Batoche, at row 7, falls just outside this band into the prairie/mountain-box rules below — see next entry.)
regions.Rockies and Selkirks chokepoint: Cols 3-10, rows 7-12. Mountain. Every one of Cochrane (7,7), Field (6,8), Calgary (8,9), Revelstoke (5,10), Gleichen (10,10), Banff (6,11), Kamloops (3,11) and Golden (5,12) lands inside this box — the single hardest and most expensive stretch of the whole railway, per the research doc's terrain section. Fort Macleod and Lethbridge (both row 13) sit deliberately just outside it: prairie/foothills towns, not mountain towns. Batoche (13,7) also falls outside this box (col 13 is past its col-10 edge), so it correctly reads as prairie/parkland rather than mountain — a real South Saskatchewan River valley town, not a Rockies one.
regions.Mountain-band chokepoint relief: (7,8), one hex directly between Cochrane and Field/Calgary, hand-converted from mountain to plains — the one change in this pass that isn't purely mechanical region-rule output. Per the required reading's own flag: the real CPR route through here is a genuine single-file chain (Field-Cochrane-Banff-Calgary-Revelstoke-Golden-Kamloops-Gleichen), and the forest/mountain 'one cube per hex, forever' rule (intentional, unchanged, shared by all three boards) means one company claiming that whole chain early can permanently wall off every rival from the Pacific coast. The Canadian board hit the same shape of problem once and fixed it the same way: turn one hinge hex from forest to plains, so a second company can route Calgary -> (8,8) [mountain, its own cube] -> (7,8) [plains, unlimited] -> Cochrane/Field, alongside whatever the first company already claimed on the strict main line -- without touching the mountain rule or removing the challenge everywhere else. This is a small, deliberately narrow fix (one hex, at the single busiest hinge of the whole corridor, per the build report's own account of a company owning 'Calgary, Cochrane, Field, Golden, Revelstoke, Banff' in one 16-game measurement) -- not a full redesign of the mountain band's shape, which the task brief explicitly allows deferring if a bigger geometry change isn't safe to combine with everything else in this pass. See docs/western-canada-board-rework-2.md for the honest scope of what this one hex does and doesn't fix.
regions.Fraser Canyon: Cols 0-3, rows 11-14. Mountain, shading toward plains at Kamloops (already in the box above). Onderdonk's Fraser Canyon contract — Yale (2,13) sits right in this band.
regions.Lower Mainland lowlands: Cols 0-3, rows 14-17. Plains. Vancouver, Port Moody, New Westminster and the near shore — flat lowland delta country opening onto the Strait of Georgia. Vancouver Island (Victoria, Esquimalt, Nanaimo) and its water-gap crossing were removed entirely in this pass; there is no island cluster or off-map strait carving left on this board.
regions.Prairie corridor: Everything else still standing (Manitoba, Saskatchewan/Assiniboia, and Alberta east of the foothills), plus Batoche's own hex (13,7), which the mountain box's column range doesn't reach. Plains — the flat-to-rolling country that let Van Horne's crews lay 500+ miles in a single season (1882).
